messages:
maya: Heads-up — we have a high-severity support escalation from AcmeCorp. Multiple customers reporting p95 generation latency >10s and intermittent 5xx/504s for hosted endpoints starting ~13:12 UTC. They attached client traces and a repro. Can oncall triage? :rotating_light:

sam: I'm on it. Can you paste a sample request/response and any request IDs? I'll start a war room if this is still ongoing.

maya: Sample request id: req_0a9f8c2. Payload: long completion with max_tokens=4096, stop tokens not hit. Attached snippet:```json
{"model":"rwd-13b-v1","prompt":"<customer prompt>","max_tokens":4096,"stream":false}
```
Response was immediate 502 with gateway error. Also seeing spikes of 504 on other requests.

incidents-bot: Deployed commit d4f7b2 to hosted-runtime at 2024-11-02T12:05:33Z (canary -> prod).

tom: Noted the deploy. I'm checking runtime metrics now — preliminary: batcher queue > 2x normal, KV cache hit rate dropped, and there are a bunch of long-running token loops. Could be one of the new kernel paths combined with huge sequence lengths causing throughput collapse.

elena: Autoscaler also shows a fast downscale event at 12:00 UTC then a burst at 13:10. Looks like a mis-tuned cooldown; we lost capacity right before the spike.

sam: Oncall checklist: (1) isolate customer traffic by routing to fallback model variant (rwd-13b-v1-small) (2) increase pool size for hosted-production temporarily (3) enable circuit-breaker to shed very large requests. Who can trigger routing?

jess: I can draft the customer message once we have a mitigation. AcmeCorp reported live timeouts during checkout flow — this is high customer impact.

maya: Repro steps from Acme: they batch multiple large completions in parallel (30 concurrent requests with max_tokens=4096). They saw growing p95 then 502s across all endpoints.

tom: OK, immediate mitigation plan: 1) add route rule to send AcmeCorp traffic and a few other top callers to smaller model variant (oncall can set) 2) roll back canary commit d4f7b2 if we see correlation 3) temporarily bump min instances to +30% in eu-west region to absorb burst. I'll start a canary rollback runbook if needed.

elena: I can bump min instances and adjust cooldown. I'll also add a temporary rate limit on large max_tokens via ingress (30s).

sam: I'll do the route rule and circuit-breaker activation now. If anyone sees >20% 5xx after that, call it out.

incidents-bot: Route rule applied: send traffic with header X-Customer-ID:AcmeCorp -> rwd-13b-v1-small at 13:28 UTC. Circuit breaker threshold set: request_cpu_ms > 5000 -> 503.

maya: Customer informed we’re applying mitigations and will follow up with root cause. They asked for an ETA — told them 60m.

jess: I'll send a customer note draft: short apology, mitigations applied, we’re investigating root cause and will share a timeline and postmortem.

tom: Early data after routing: 5xx count for Acme down from 18% -> 2% in the last 5m. Overall platform 5xx still elevated but trending down. We should keep routing in place while investigating logs.

sam: Logs: seeing a sharp increase in per-token CPU and repeated GC-like stalls in the rwd-13b-v1 build after deploy d4f7b2. Not seeing auth/billing errors. Looks runtime/efficiency related, not auth.

maya: Support note: several customers also mentioned request latency leaking into their client timeouts (client side retries amplified the problem). We should tighten the recommended client retry guidelines in the interim.

elena: Action items so far: elena -> bump capacity and cooldown (done), sam -> applied route rule + circuit breaker (done), tom -> gather flamegraphs and kernel traces for deploy d4f7b2 (in progress), maya/jess -> customer comms and recommended retry guidance (in progress).

tom: Quick grep of host logs shows these repeated entries:
```
[2024-11-02T13:14:02Z] req=0a9f8c2 worker=gw-12 queue_wait_ms=5400 kv_hit=false model=rwd-13b-v1 tokens_processed=1200 cpu_ms=6200 -> gateway_502
[2024-11-02T13:15:16Z] req=0b3c7a1 worker=gw-10 queue_wait_ms=6100 kv_hit=false model=rwd-13b-v1 tokens_processed=1400 cpu_ms=6800 -> gateway_504
```
These lines point at long queue waits and CPU pressure per-request.

sam: Given that, I recommend a rollback of d4f7b2 for the runtime path if traces confirm a kernel regression. tom, can you correlate kernel module versions and CPU profile with the long requests?

tom: Will do. If rollback is needed we'll follow rollback runbook. We should also add a mitigation short-term: auto-split large requests (if max_tokens > 2048) into streaming partials to avoid huge single-request CPU spikes. Ops feasibility check: elena?

elena: Auto-splitting at the gateway is feasible as a temporary hack but needs careful semantic preservation. Short-term we can enforce max_tokens=2048 policy for hosted API customers as a protective action, with opt-in exceptions.

jess: Customer-facing plan: (1) immediate: we applied routing + increased capacity, shared ETA 60m (2) short-term: tighten max_tokens to 2048 and recommend streaming for large completions (3) long-term: postmortem and rollback/patch + improved autoscaler tuning. I'll get approvals for the message.

maya: Postmortem expectations: timeline, root cause (kernel/regression vs autoscaler cooldown vs customer behaviour), impact table (customers affected), mitigations, and actions: rollback/patch, default max_tokens cap, autoscaler cooldown fix, kernel path testing harness, and docs update for client retry guidance.

sam: Agree. I'll tag this for a 1hr blameless postmortem meeting 2024-11-03 16:00 UTC and assign owners.

tom: For now, monitoring: keep routing + breakers on, track 5xx and p95 every 5m. I'll upload flamegraphs and kernel traces to the incident folder when ready.

elena: Also adding a pinned note to infra runbook to prevent simultaneous aggressive downscale during high request variance windows.

maya: Thanks all — keep updates short here. jess/maya will finalize customer comms. Will post postmortem link once scheduled. :thumbsup:
